abstract: Kulveit, Soares, and coauthors argue that even absent a discrete misaligned-AGI event, incremental AI capability gains can produce gradual systemic disempowerment of humans — through erosion of labor income (humans no longer needed economically), political representation (decisions delegated to AI), and culture (AI-mediated information environments). Each step is locally rational; the cumulative trajectory is not.
keyFindings: Frames existential risk as a gradual systems-level erosion rather than a discrete catastrophe
Identifies three reinforcing channels: economic (labor displacement), political (delegation), and cultural (info environment)
Argues incentive structures of incremental AI deployment select against human leverage even with no malicious actor
Influential in AI safety / governance circles concerned with non-misalignment failure modes
methodology: Conceptual analysis; identifies feedback loops rather than estimates magnitudes.
qualifiers: Tier 2 working paper (arXiv 2501.16946). Not peer-reviewed at submission. Mechanistically rich but not quantitatively calibrated; treat as a framework for risk identification, not as a forecast.
